verdict:
X-band edge guidance reduced accuracy. Relative to a control given the same extra training, arm B lost 0.21 SSIM points across 152 test tiles (Wilcoxon p < 0.001). SSIM fell on all 48 Houston tiles, by 0.24 points in Owens (p = 0.003) and by 0.15 in Western Australia (p = 0.014). Missed-edge distances improved by 0.4–1.2 m, but ENL fell from 200 to 166 and agreement with held-out X-band edges did not improve. We kept X-band out of the final training loss.

The baseline’s main benefit was despeckling. ESRT raised SSIM from 35.2 to 41.7 and PSNR from 21.0 to 22.0 dB over bicubic. Lee filtering followed by bicubic reached 39.3 and 21.7 dB. Fine-detail correlation increased only from 0.070 to 0.086, and the energy ratio was 0.20, indicating substantially smoother output than Stripmap. These selected-tile scores cannot be compared directly with the paper’s whole-scene scores.
data: We processed 71 Stripmap scenes: 48 pilot scenes, 13 replacements and the paper’s 10 scenes. Each tile uses sarsen terrain-flattened gamma0 on a 5 m grid, with an EGM2008 geoid correction. IW is aligned first at 10 m and then at 5 m; only IW is resampled. A tile keeps its own offset when correlation is at least 0.4 and it agrees with its scene offset within 10 m. Scenes with fewer than two reliable tiles are excluded, and WorldCover water pixels are masked. Houston, Owens, Western Australia and the paper’s three test scenes are held out. Validation uses the paper’s two validation scenes and about 15% of tile locations in training regions.
geoloc:
The initial Houston tile had two processing errors. South-up sarsen output was written to a north-up grid without flipping, reducing correlation with IW to 0.08 and producing a false apparent shift of 500–800 m. Flipping raised correlation to 0.51 near zero offset. Separately, sarsen expects ellipsoidal DEM heights; adding the EGM2008 geoid correction removed a roughly 55 m range shift in Houston.

After correction, median offsets were (−8, +2) m for 17 Sentinel-1A scenes, (−5, +2) m for 20 Sentinel-1C scenes and (−16, −1) m for 5 Sentinel-1D scenes. The paper’s older scenes had offsets of 2–25 m. We found no evidence of a Sentinel-1C/1D azimuth timing bias in these data. Timor retained a stable roughly 55 m offset removed by registration. Owens had the largest within-scene spread, 17–22 m, making its detail scores less certain. Two commissioning-period IW pairings failed; Houston was re-paired and Fogo was dropped.
arma: Arm A compares three models trained on 200 tiles for 8,000 steps at batch 16: ESRT with the paper’s SSIM and histogram-matching recipe, ESRT with an additional input-consistency term, and a residual CNN with consistency. Input patches are 48 × 48 pixels and targets are 96 × 96. The Stripmap target is Lee-filtered and histogram-matched to IW, with global 0.1/99.9 percentile normalization. The consistency term uses L2 at weight 0.15 after averaging output back to 10 m. The three models score within 0.3 SSIM points.
metrics: SSIM and PSNR are computed in the paper's space: [0, 1] min-max dB against the histogram-matched reference, either Lee-filtered (the paper's) or raw. MAE is in dB. Detail r is the correlation of the 5 m detail layer (image minus its 10 m block mean) with Stripmap's, and the HF ratio is its energy relative to Stripmap's. Edge distances use the same Canny detector on prediction and Stripmap (m, capped at 50). ENL, MoI, MoR and Cx are measured on the two most homogeneous 32 × 32 windows per tile, in linear intensity, against the IW input. Stripmap rows show the reference's own ENL and Cx.
stage1:
The X-band comparison measures edge distances on infrastructure, using OSM roads and buildings or WorldCover built-up pixels. Masks exclude water, detected change, slopes over 20°, layover and shadow where available. One set contains 126 X-band acquisitions more than 150 km from training tiles; 85 have enough infrastructure to score. The other contains held-out Stripmap tiles overlapping Umbra or ICEYE. Capella’s Baytown images fall outside the Houston Stripmap swath and enter only the first set. X-band is registered to IW, not Stripmap.

Real Stripmap has an output-to-X-band edge distance of 24.1 m, versus 23.7 m for bicubic IW. In the reverse direction it improves from 31.5 to 27.9 m. Thus, even the real C-band reference has limited edge agreement with X-band. Different wavelength, date and viewing geometry matter; only 18% of Houston pairs match Stripmap geometry within 5°. Model improvements of about 1–2 m over bicubic are consistent with reduced speckle, but do not establish recovered 5 m structure.
armb: Arm B adds an edge-distance loss to ESRT for 3,000 steps. Distances within 5 m are unpenalized and the penalty saturates at 20 m. The loss applies only to infrastructure, with water, change, layover and shadow masked. A quarter of each batch uses X-band pairs: 87 ICEYE, 70 Umbra and 16 Capella. The control receives the same extra steps without edge loss. Only 15% of these pairs registered to IW; the rest rely on provider geolocation. Validation selected weight 0.05, which tied the control at SSIM 0.4127; weight 0.2 scored 0.4124. The held-out comparison appears above.
panels: Each comparison shows a 9.6 km IW window around a test tile, plus a 1.6 km close-up beside Stripmap. Additional windows cover Iowa farmland, Rondônia forest, the Swiss Alps, Saharan dunes, Nile Delta villages and Pamplona. The models reduce speckle and clarify some existing edges. ESRT arms A and B look similar. Windows without Stripmap are visual checks; their appearance does not establish accuracy.
caveats:
• We evaluate selected 3.2 km tiles with different processing from the paper. Compare model rankings within this evaluation, not absolute scores across studies.
  • Training ran 8,000 steps at batch 16 on a GPU shared with three other experiments, against the paper's 30 epochs at batch 128 over 436k patches. Validation SSIM rose by under 0.005 after step 5,000.
  • Round 1 has no IW-to-Stripmap change mask. Round 3 tests an approximate mask from bracketing same-track IW dates; it does not improve the overall result.
  • The Lee filter is a classic 7×7 Lee with looks estimated per tile (about 2.5 to 3), close to SNAP's but not identical. Co-registration is a global shift per tile, not Gefolki's dense flow.
  • X-band layover masks use an approximate look azimuth (right-looking, from orbit direction) where the item gives none. Most training X-band pairs did not register to the IW.
  • Owens' registration is the noisiest of the holdouts (17 to 22 m spread within a scene).
